analysis: The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts (lines 25221-26796) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json, a golden-vector test fixture holding gemma-4-26b-qat-4bit vectors. They contain request bodies, provider bodies, template inputs, plans (prompt_contract_id, block-boundary chain hashes) and token_ids. The base lines are mostly outside the changed ranges, which sit around base 3024-4003, 4824, 43813-45533 and 52418-54138. The visible patch excerpt is truncated. It shows a qwen-style vector gaining additional_context.enable_thinking=false, a token count change from 803 to 767, and updated chain hashes. Only test data and expected values change, with no executable code, key handling, auth, attestation, encryption or routing logic. No new network surface, secrets or credentials appear in the excerpts. The vectors carry no real consumer data; the dates and strings are synthetic. Prompt-cache concerns (T-041) relate to chain-hash and prompt_contract_id semantics. This change only regenerates fixture expectations and does not alter the cache keying code visible here. I cannot verify that the new hashes match the Swift and Go implementations, or that the corresponding producer code changes (additional_context handling) are safe, because that source is outside this batch. The integration pass should check that the source change that adds additional_context/enable_thinking does not alter cache scoping or leak across tenants. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.
